subject: Mid-term renewal: rebalancing reserved GPU buckets & throughput SLOs for QuantaCorp
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@quantacorp.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-15T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-year capacity rebalance request / pricing options

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the renewal paperwork last month. We kicked off a new internal initiative that will run heavy batch inference for two weeks every month starting October. The pattern means we need to shift some of our reserved commit from steady baseline to a burstable bucket that guarantees higher throughput for short windows.

Specific ask: can Redwood propose a mid-term amendment that: (1) adds ~60 T4-equivalent slots usable as a burst pool for 2x throughput windows, (2) preserves our base throughput SLA, and (3) shows cost delta vs just buying an extra steady commit? Also include any discounts for adding during a renewal period and whether we can apply unused credits from our current commitment.

We need a ballpark by Monday to raise in procurement. Attaching our rough capacity plan.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Liu
Director, Platform Engineering
QuantaCorp

Attachment: capacity-plan-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@quantacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-15T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-year capacity rebalance request / pricing options

Hi Sara — appreciate the context and the plan. Quick summary of feasible approaches and tradeoffs: 

1) Top-up burst pool (recommended for short, predictable spikes)
   - Add a burst pool of 60 T4-equivalent slots available for up to 48 hours per month.
   - Pricing: incremental monthly fee = reserved uplift price prorated + burst premium (~18% on top of steady commit).
   - Pros: fast to enable, no long-term change in baseline commit.
   - Cons: higher unit cost for burst tokens; subject to burst availability if other customers also burst.

2) Reprofile commit into buckets (best for predictable recurring windows)
   - Reallocate part of your existing commit into two buckets: Baseline (70%) and Burst (30%).
   - Pricing: overall commit price roughly neutral if we smooth pricing across buckets; could reduce wasted idle capacity.
   - Pros: better economics than repeat top-ups; capacity guaranteed by contract.
   - Cons: requires mid-term amendment to contract and run-rate smoothing.

3) Step-up reserved commit (longer-term growth)
   - Add a dedicated, steady commit for incremental throughput; lower per-unit cost but you pay for capacity continuously.

Discount/credits options we can consider:
- Mid-term amendment discount: we can offer a one-time 5-8% concession on the incremental commit if Quanta re-commits for at least 9 months of the new capacity.
- Apply unused credits: we can credit remaining committed spend against the first 2 months of incremental fees.

I attached a quick cost sketch and a proposed amendment (proposed_amendment_qc_v2.pdf) that lays out the reprofile approach with two scenarios. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through numbers.

Next steps from our side: I’ll loop Marissa to get a formal quote and packet for procurement and confirm discount authority.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_amendment_qc_v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB); capacity-plan-v2.xlsx referenced

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-16T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Mid-year capacity rebalance request / pricing options

Vivek — reviewed. Authorization guidance: we can approve up to a 6% one-time concession on incremental reserved commit for a 9-month minimum on the uplift. If they convert the burst pool into steady commit at renewal we can ladder an additional 3% credit back as a retention incentive.

Packaging suggestion:
- Option A (short term, predictable bursts): implement Top-up burst for Oct-Dec, charge premium, apply unused credits for first two months. No contract change required.
- Option B (recommended economics): reprofile 30% to Burst buckets via amendment; apply 6% concession on incremental dollars; amendment term to align with existing renewal date (Feb 2027).

Please include precise monthly numbers in the quote and call out SLO impact (we keep baseline SLA; burst SLO is best-effort with priority routing and optional guaranteed burst windows if they accept reprofile).

Marissa
Account Director, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@quantacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-year capacity rebalance request / pricing options

Hi Sara — following up with concrete numbers based on your attachment. Summary of the two scenarios we recommend (spreadsheet attached):

Scenario 1 — Top-up burst (fastest)
- 60 T4-equivalent burst pool available 48 hrs/month
- Estimated incremental monthly fee: $28,500 (burst premium applied)
- One-time admin amendment: $0 (no contract change)
- Discount: apply remaining credits to first 2 months (savings ~ $6.2k)

Scenario 2 — Reprofile commit into Baseline/Burst buckets (recommended)
- Move ~30% of current commit into a Burst bucket + add 20% new commit to reduce peak cost
- Net incremental monthly fee: $14,400 after 6% concession (9-month min on uplift)
- Amendment required; guaranteed burst windows defined in Exhibit A (we included windows you requested)

Attached: capacity-plan-v2.xlsx (numbers) and proposed_amendment_qc_v2.pdf (redlines). If procurement wants legal redlines, we can ingest and turn around within 3 business days.

Tell me a good time tomorrow (30 min) and I’ll have Marissa on the call to finalize concession and packaging.

Thanks,
Vivek
